commands.review_summary:
The PR stamps the originating workflow URL into new apply-health snapshots, makes dashboard cards prefer that immutable URL over the mutable root status URL, and adds a focused precedence regression assertion.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection shows a retained apply-health snapshot can be paired with a later mutable root run URL, and the production screenshot plus linked run metadata corroborate the resulting misleading dashboard action.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] The contributor must provide real after-fix behavior proof and remove the release-owned changelog entry; ClawSweeper automation cannot create proof from the contributor’s setup.

target.title: fix(dashboard): link apply health cards to source runs
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep each apply-health dashboard alert linked to the workflow run that generated that health snapshot.
- Preserve the old top-level status link as a compatibility fallback for existing snapshots.

## Problem

The dashboard stores an apply-health snapshot while subsequent review/status writes update the top-level `run_url`. The "Pruning sweep blocked" card therefore kept the original apply warning but opened a later, unrelated review run. In the captured production case, the card linked to [run 29091926566](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091926566), a successful hot-review run whose apply job was skipped; it was not the run that produced the one-record apply-health warning.

![Dashboard alert pointing at an unrelated workflow run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/codex/fix-apply-health-link/docs/proof/dashboard-apply-health-run-link/mislinked-apply-health-alert.png)

## Implementation

- Stamp `run_url` into a newly written apply-health snapshot.
- Have the dashboard read that immutable health-snapshot URL first, then fall back to the mutable root status URL for older snapshots.
- Add a regression assertion covering a newer top-level status link alongside an older apply-health link.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:all`
- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` (62 passing)
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check dashboard/worker.ts src/clawsweeper.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

`pnpm run format:check` reports pre-existing repository-wide formatting issues; the direct check above passes for every touched source file. `pnpm run test:coverage:changed` exceeded the local two-minute command window without returning a failure, so it is not claimed as passing.

## Review closeout

Manual source review found the apply workflow already passes its current workflow URL when publishing each apply-health snapshot. The automated Codex review command could not start because this machine's local Codex CLI configuration has an incompatible `service_tier` value; a one-off override was rejected by the service. No review findings were accepted.

## Risks and rollout

New snapshots gain a nested source URL. Existing snapshots continue using the present top-level URL fallback, so the change is backward compatible. It changes dashboard observability only; it does not alter sweep, comment, label, or close behavior.

## Links

- Production UI evidence: [run 29091926566](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091926566)
- The displayed apply warning was a safe one-record `kept_open` skip, not a global backlog/apply failure.
